note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Calculate a student's grade point average: the course grade points weighted by course credits. Round the result to 2 decimals using round half to even, as the registrar does: a value exactly halfway rounds to the even last digit.
facts: Made-up examples: grade points 3.7 (3 credits), 3.3 (3 credits) and 2.0 (2 credits) give 25 / 8 = 3.125, which rounds to 3.12. Grade points 4.0, 3.0, 2.0 and 1.7 at 1 credit each give 2.675, which rounds to 2.68. A student with no credits has no GPA.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: GPA = sum of (course grade points x course credits) divided by the sum of course credits, over all of the student's courses.
REQ-2: Round the GPA to 2 decimals using round half to even: a value exactly halfway between two 2-decimal values rounds to the one whose last digit is even.
REQ-3: Use exact decimal arithmetic, not binary floating point. In binary, 2.675 is stored slightly below 2.675, so a float would round it to 2.67 instead of 2.68.
REQ-4: If the student has zero total credits, return no GPA. Do not return 0.00 and do not divide by zero.
AC-1: Grade points 3.7 (3 credits), 3.3 (3 credits) and 2.0 (2 credits) give (11.1 + 9.9 + 4.0) / 8 = 25 / 8 = 3.125, which rounds to 3.12 because 2 is even.
AC-2: Grade points 4.0, 3.0, 2.0 and 1.7 at 1 credit each give 10.7 / 4 = 2.675, which rounds to 2.68 because 8 is even. A result of 2.67 fails this check.
AC-3: A student with no credits gets no GPA. A result of 0.00 or an error fails this check.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: GPA equals the sum of each course grade points times its credits, divided by total credits.
REQ-2: Round the GPA to 2 decimals with round half to even: a value exactly halfway rounds to the even last digit.
REQ-3: A student with no credits has no GPA.
AC-1: Grade points 3.7 (3 credits), 3.3 (3 credits) and 2.0 (2 credits) give 25/8 = 3.125, which rounds to 3.12.
AC-2: Grade points 4.0, 3.0, 2.0 and 1.7 at 1 credit each give 2.675, which rounds to 2.68.
AC-3: A student with no credits has no GPA.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft correctly weights both examples, including 25/8 = 3.125 to 3.12 and 10.7/4 = 2.675 to 2.68, and it withholds a GPA when total credits are zero.

findings.title: Exact decimal arithmetic not required
findings.detail: 2.675 cannot be stored exactly in binary floating point (about 2.67499999). A float-based implementation would return 2.67 and fail AC-2. REQ-2 should require exact decimal arithmetic, with rounding applied only to the final quotient.
findings.quote: REQ-2: Round the GPA to 2 decimals with round half to even: a value exactly halfway rounds to the even last digit.

findings.title: AC-3 not testable as written
findings.detail: AC-3 repeats REQ-3 word for word. It does not say what a tester should observe, such as no value returned and no division by zero. The expected outcome is left implicit.
findings.quote: AC-3: A student with no credits has no GPA.

reviewOfB.strengths: Both worked examples check out: 3.7×3 + 3.3×3 + 2.0×2 = 25, and 25/8 = 3.125 rounds to 3.12; 10.7/4 = 2.675 rounds to 2.68 under round half to even.

build.contract: calculateGpa(input) where input = { courses: Array<{ gradePoints, credits }> }. gradePoints and credits must be decimal strings such as "3.7" or "3", each read as its exact decimal value; arithmetic uses exact decimals, never binary floating point. GPA = sum of (gradePoints x credits) / sum of credits, rounded once, on the final quotient only, to 2 decimals using round half to even. Returns { gpa: string | null }, where gpa is the GPA as a decimal string with exactly 2 decimals (such as "3.12" or "2.68"), or null when total credits are zero, including an empty courses array. In that case no division occurs, and it never returns "0.00" in place of null. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input or any course has any other field. Throws an Error whose message is "invalid decimal: <name>" if gradePoints or credits is not a decimal string, including when it is a number.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure module exporting calculateGpa(input) -> { gpa: string | null }, with no I/O and no dependencies, implementing REQ-1 to REQ-4 and the contract exactly.
Validation: reject any key on input other than courses, and any key on a course other than gradePoints and credits, with Error("unknown field: <name>"). Each value must be a string matching ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$; anything else, including a number or a missing value, throws Error("invalid decimal: <name>").
Data: parse each decimal string into an exact scaled integer (BigInt digits plus a scale). Never call parseFloat or Number, so REQ-3 holds and 2.675 stays exact.
Compute: N = sum of gradePoints x credits and D = sum of credits, both kept as exact scaled integers on a common scale. Nothing is rounded at this stage.
Zero case: if D = 0, including an empty courses array or all courses at 0 credits, return { gpa: null } before any division. Never return "0.00" (REQ-4, AC-3).
Rounding, done once on the final quotient: q = floor(N x 100 / D) and r = remainder. Round up if 2r > D. On an exact tie (2r = D), round up only if q is odd. Format q / 100 with exactly 2 decimals. This stays exact even for quotients that do not terminate, such as 10/3.
Verified by hand: AC-1 is 25.0 / 8 = 3.125, which ties and gives "3.12" (2 is even). AC-2 is 10.7 / 4 = 2.675, which ties and gives "2.68" (8 is even). AC-3 gives null.
Tests: AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3; an empty courses array; all courses at 0 credits; an unknown field on input and on a course; numeric 3.7 rejected; a non-terminating quotient.
File fence, the only files that may change: src/gpa.js (new) and test/gpa.test.js (new). The names are proposed; adjust them to the repo layout.
Open points: the behavior when courses is missing or is not an array is unspecified, and the contract does not set any upper bound on grade points.

code.summary:
The module is a single expression that returns { calculateGpa }. It uses only exact BigInt scaled-integer arithmetic and never calls parseFloat or Number.

Validation: an unknown key on the input or on a course throws "unknown field: <name>". A gradePoints or credits value that is not a string matching ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ throws "invalid decimal: <name>". That includes numbers and missing values.

Calculation: N (the sum of grade points times credits) and D (the sum of credits) are both accumulated exactly. If D is 0, which covers an empty array and courses that all have zero credits, the result is { gpa: null } and no division happens.

Rounding happens once, on the final quotient. Let q = floor(N*100/D) and r be the remainder. The result rounds up if 2r > D, or if 2r = D and q is odd. It is then formatted with exactly 2 decimals.

Hand-checked:
- AC-1: 25000/80 gives q=312 with a tie, and q is even, so the result is "3.12".
- AC-2: 10700/40 gives q=267 with a tie, and q is odd, so the result is "2.68".
- AC-3: the result is null.

Open points resolved by assumption, since none are in the contract:
- An input that is not an object throws "invalid input".
- A missing or non-array courses value throws "invalid courses".
- A course that is not an object throws "invalid course".
- Negative values are rejected by the pattern.
- No upper bound is placed on grade points.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Exact BigInt decimals round only the final quotient half-to-even, so 3.125 becomes 3.12 and 2.675 becomes 2.68, and zero credits returns null without dividing.
code.resolutions: Review: no defects found; exact BigInt decimals, half-to-even on final quotient only, null for zero credits. applied: Agreed after checking it myself; code left unchanged. AC-1: N=250 (scale 1), D=8, so num=25000 and den=80. That gives q=312 with remainder exactly half, and 312 is even, so the result is 3.12. AC-2: N=107 (scale 1), D=4, so num=10700 and den=40. That gives q=267 with remainder exactly half, and 267 is odd, so it rounds up to 2.68. AC-3: zero or empty credits return null before any division. Numbers are rejected with 'invalid decimal: <name>'. Unknown keys raise 'unknown field: <name>'. Small results pad correctly, for example 0.05.

diagram.summary: A calling system reads a student's course records and passes grade points and credits as decimal strings to a new GPA module in src/gpa.js; the module validates and parses them exactly, sums credit-weighted points and credits, then either returns null when credits are zero or returns a GPA rounded half to even to 2 decimals.
